A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPT policy-gradient research despite the changed title. Their complete 52-page contents, including equations, figures, tables and reordered appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original CPT-PG simulations in Section 5 and Appendix K, including bandits, grid environments, electricity management, financial trading and MuJoCo.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix J, together with the relocated RiskyGridworld comparison in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The CPT objective, order-statistic estimator, Algorithm 1 updates and alternative piecewise-weight procedure are retained. Theorem 3's revised formula is not accompanied by a documented change to the algorithm or experimental implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same gain/loss bandits, custom gridworlds, traffic control, electricity management, BTC-USD trading and InvertedPendulum-v5 environments. Reordered appendices introduce no additional evaluated domains or tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain vanilla PG, exponential risk-sensitive PG and CPT-SPSA-G comparisons. The newly cited DRM policy-gradient and Newton methods appear in research discussions, not in added experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: The retained experiments use the same reported rewards, metrics, training budgets, batch sizes and hyperparameters, including grid sizes 3, 5 and 9. Explicitly specifying the bandit reference point in v4 adds documentation without establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: Batch-size sensitivity, stochastic-policy behavior, Markovian versus non-Markovian comparisons, and utility/reference-point analyses were already present in v3. The additional Section 5 remarks discuss retained analyses.

E5.justification: Run counts and uncertainty practices are retained, including five-seed bandit comparisons, ten-run grid comparisons and median/25–75% reporting for finance and MuJoCo. Figure 15 corrects 'interquantile' to 'interquartile' while retaining the same band and 100 runs.

E6.justification: Matched figures retain the same learning curves, policy visualizations and reported outcomes, including the grid-scaling comparison, electricity-return distributions and MuJoCo results. No empirical result entries or rankings are added, removed or changed.

T1.justification: Theorem 3 replaces raw-return integration limits max(v,0) and max(-v,0) with u+(R(tau)) and u-(R(tau)), correcting the stated utility dependence. Section 2.1 also corrects the endpoint condition to w+(1)=w-(1)=1. The appendix proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The theorem, algorithm and convergence contributions remain, but v4 removes the explicit claim of being the first such algorithm and foregrounds DRM special cases. The abstract and introduction describe the empirical contribution more cautiously, with scalability comparisons qualified by the simulation settings.

C2.justification: v4 expands the explanation of coupled gain/loss weighting in DRMs versus CPT's flexibility. It also adds qualifications concerning memory and higher-dimensional scaling, and makes misuse through user manipulation an explicit concern in the revised Broader Impact Statement.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly specifies x0=0 for the bandit experiments. Much of the added history-window discussion already appeared in v3 Appendix K; hardware, software, hyperparameter tables and substantive access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Vijayan and L.A. (2024) and Pachal et al. (2025), explaining connections to first-order DRM gradients and distinctions from Newton methods. This refines the closest-work positioning while retaining the broader CPT, risk-sensitive and convex-RL discussion.

P1.justification: v4 retitles the paper, rewrites the abstract and conclusion, revises introductory framing and adds numbered experimental remarks. It substantially reorganizes the appendices, bringing proofs forward and moving the rewritten Broader Impact Statement into the main document.

P2.justification: The same 26 figures and four tables are retained. Changes chiefly involve relocation and renumbering, altered float placement, displaying the gradient-weight formula separately, and limited caption corrections; the plotted graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves precision through the corrected Theorem 3 integration limits, explicit acknowledgment of related first-order DRM work, and more qualified novelty and application claims. These provide a limited overall gain in clarity and positioning; the algorithm, substantive proofs and empirical evidence remain largely unchanged.
